description: WebSocket message vectors. Spec: docs/protocol.md, "Control channel: WebSocket". valid[] and invalid[] cases are independent; sequences[] run in order on one connection that starts before hello.
howToRead: from = sender role (phone or pc), to = receiver role. state = "before_hello" (receiver has not seen a hello yet) or "open". Input is one of: frame (a JSON object, serialize compactly), raw (a text frame, send exactly this string), rawHex (a text frame with exactly these payload bytes, hex), binaryHex (a binary frame), synthesize ({ base, field, fill, fillCount, totalBytes }: take base, set base[field] to fill repeated fillCount times, serialize compactly in key order; the result is exactly totalBytes UTF-8 bytes). expect.reply = ack (receiver sends { type: ack, ref: frame.id }) | error (receiver sends { type: error, code, ref } and ref is omitted when null) | none. expect.close = WebSocket close code the receiver then uses, or null to stay open. expect.action is the category of what the receiver does: handshake_ok, mark_delivered, mark_failed, show_error_only, deliver_text, set_clipboard, start_download, mark_transfer_done, cancel_transfer, remove_peer_and_close, show_ping_toast, ignore_duplicate, close_only. raw may hold escapes that a JSON value cannot express (duplicate keys, lone surrogate escapes such as the six characters backslash u d 8 0 0): send the string exactly as written. expect.ref on an ack pins the id the ack points at. expect.sensitive on a deliver_text case says whether the receiver treats the text as sensitive (the optional sensitive field is true); absent means false. timers[] and closeCodes[] are about time and client behaviour, not frames: see their own fields. A closeCodes[] case may also carry helloAcceptedForMs (how long the peer's hello had been accepted when the connection ended, null if none ever was) and resetsBackoff (true only from 60000 ms on): the backoff resets only after a connection stayed open with an accepted hello for at least 60 s. raw cases named strict-* and nesting-* are invalid JSON for the protocol (unquoted literals, 01, NaN, nesting deeper than 64): bad_request with no ref. A media.* case (changelog 57) lists own and peer, the capabilities of the receiver's own latest hello and of the sender's latest hello: the message is dropped silently (action media_dropped, no reply) unless both list media, and so is a media.image whose picture fails its checks. expect.media is what the receiver ends up with after cleaning: every media.state has rateMilli (default 1000) and actions (canonical order, unknown entries and an unbelievable seek removed); an absent optional string, number or object is left out. No media.* message is acked or remembered. An alert case (changelog 59, PC to phone) lists own and peer like the others, but the capability is the SENDER's rule: the receiver acks every valid alert (action deliver_alert, expect.alert = the text and title cleaned like link.title and cut to 300 / 60 code points, waitedMs cut to 7 days), de-duplicates by id (ignore_duplicate), answers too_large over 4096 bytes, and answers rate_limited with ref when alertBudgetSpent is true (the phone's bucket is empty: checked after the fields and the duplicate rule, and not remembered). A sequence step may set alertBudgetSpent for the receiver of that step.

sequences.name: alert-is-queued-and-acked
sequences.note: an alert that waited in the PC's queue arrives after the next hellos like any other item, with how long it waited (clock-independent), and is acked

sequences.name: alert-repeat-gets-the-first-answer
sequences.note: a re-queued alert (no ack in 5 s, or after a reconnect) carries the same id: the repeat is acked again and nothing is shown twice

sequences.name: alert-rate-limited-fails-the-item
sequences.note: an error rate_limited with ref fails that item on the PC, is not remembered, and a later alert is accepted once the bucket has a token

sequences.name: alert-quiet-when-paused
sequences.note: a paused phone acks and stores the alert like any other: it only shows nothing (history row, counted); the wire is the same, which is why the PC's own pause check for event-driven alerts is the PC's (PAUSED_SKIPPED)

sequences.name: alert-capability-is-the-senders-rule
sequences.note: the PC sends an alert only to a phone whose latest hello lists alert (alertSend[]: otherwise the item fails locally as peer_unsupported and nothing is sent, never a text). A receiver that understands alert handles one that reaches it, whatever its own hello said

sequences.name: alert-expires-locally
sequences.note: expiry is the sender's and local: nothing about it crosses the wire. After the expired alert (never sent, alertSend[]) the next hellos carry only the alert that is still alive, and the receiver never sees the expired id

sequences.name: handshake-then-text-then-duplicate
sequences.note: a repeat of an id gets the same ack and is not processed again

sequences.name: rejected-message-id-is-not-remembered
sequences.note: an invalid message is not processed, so the same id may be sent again with a corrected body

sequences.name: second-hello-after-handshake-is-a-normal-message
sequences.note: a hello is only special as the first message; later it is just a known type (no ack, no dedup)

sequences.name: invalid-hello-does-not-count-as-accepted
sequences.note: a hello that fails validation leaves the receiver before hello, so the next non-hello closes with 1002

sequences.name: garbage-before-hello-keeps-the-connection-open
sequences.note: first frames that are not a JSON object with a string type get bad_request and the connection stays open; a good hello then works

sequences.name: future-hello-gets-unsupported-version-not-a-timeout
sequences.note: protocol 2 with a different shape is answered with unsupported_version and 4002 straight away

sequences.name: same-pc-repeat-after-done-is-acked
sequences.note: changelog 52: the same paired PC repeats an offer whose download is DONE (the phone finished it, its complete may not have been acked, and the PC re-sent its queue after a reconnect). It is a repeat whatever the state of the download: the phone answers with the first response, the stored ack, downloads nothing again, and re-sends its complete if that was not acked. It is not bad_request

steps.note: the connection died; the PC never saw the ack, so it re-sends the offer after its hello

sequences.name: same-pc-repeat-after-canceled-is-acked
sequences.note: changelog 52: the same repeat for an offer that was CANCELED or FAILED on the phone: acked with the first response, nothing downloaded, and the phone re-sends its cancel (it keeps it until it is acked). Never bad_request

sequences.name: offer-from-another-device-is-bad-request
sequences.note: changelog 52: an offer with the ID of an offer that ANOTHER paired PC made is a reuse: error bad_request with ref = the offer id, and nothing is started. A transfer ID belongs to the device that made it. The first PC can still repeat its own offer afterwards

steps.note: a connection from a second paired PC

sequences.name: same-pc-repeat-with-different-files-is-bad-request
sequences.note: changelog 52, optional: a repeat from the same PC that lists other fileIds or other sizes than the first offer is not a repeat of it: error bad_request with ref = the offer id (the stored list stays). Names and MIME types are not compared. A receiver may skip this check

sequences.name: complete-re-sent-after-reconnect-is-acked-again
sequences.note: changelog 52: a complete is kept until it is acked and sent again, with the same message id, after every hello. The PC (which receives complete) acks the repeat with the first answer and does not mark the transfer done twice

steps.note: the ack of the complete was lost

sequences.name: cancel-re-sent-after-reconnect-is-acked-again
sequences.note: changelog 52: the same for a cancel, from either side: kept until acked, sent again with the same message id after every hello, and the receiver acks the repeat with its first answer without cancelling twice

steps.note: the ack of the cancel was lost

sequences.name: offer-reusing-a-text-id-is-bad-request
sequences.note: the ID space is shared: an offer whose id was already used by another message (a text here) is a reuse, not a repeat of that text, and gets error bad_request with ref = the offer id. The text is not acked or delivered a second time

sequences.name: offer-repeated-while-unfinished-is-acked-after-a-reconnect
sequences.note: changelog 52: the same paired PC re-offers an offer that is not over (it re-sent its queue, because the ack never reached it): acked as a repeat, and the phone carries on with that download. A repeat after the download is over is acked too: see same-pc-repeat-after-done-is-acked

steps.note: the connection died before the PC saw the ack; the PC reconnects and sends its queue again

sequences.name: queue-resend-after-reconnect-is-idempotent
sequences.note: a queued text is re-sent with the same id after a reconnect: the receiver repeats its first ack and does not deliver it twice. The queue goes out in creation order (A, B, C)

steps.note: the ack of B was lost: no ack in 5 s, so B goes back to queued

sequences.name: queue-is-not-sent-before-hello
sequences.note: after a reconnect nothing else goes out before the hellos: a text before the hello is bad_request and the 1002 close, and its id is not remembered, so the queue sends it again on the next connection

steps.note: the 1002 close ended it; the next connection does the hellos first

sequences.name: link-duplicate-is-acked-not-redelivered
sequences.note: a repeat of a link id gets the same ack and the link is not opened or stored twice

sequences.name: link-rejected-id-is-not-remembered
sequences.note: an invalid link is not processed, so its id is free: the corrected link with the same id is delivered

sequences.name: link-after-reconnect-is-idempotent
sequences.note: a queued link is re-sent with the same id after a reconnect (the first ack was lost): the receiver repeats its first ack and does not open it again

sequences.name: link-sent-as-text-to-an-old-peer-is-a-text
sequences.note: a peer without the link capability gets the same item as a text (same id, isUrl true, no title); it is delivered as a text. This is what the receiver of a 0.1.x app does with it

sequences.name: notif-dropped-when-feature-off-is-silent
sequences.note: the PC's switch is off, so its hello has no notif: a post is dropped with no reply at all, and nothing is shown

sequences.name: notif-capability-changes-with-a-new-hello
sequences.note: the user turns the switch on while the phone is connected: the PC sends a new hello with notif, and posts are accepted from then on (and dropped again when it is turned off)

sequences.name: notif-not-sent-without-capability-receiver-side
sequences.note: a phone that did not list notif is never obeyed: its post is dropped, whatever the PC's own setting

sequences.name: notif-is-not-in-the-dedup-memory
sequences.note: a repeated id of an ephemeral message is processed again: no ack, no ignore_duplicate

sequences.name: notif-action-is-acked-and-a-repeat-is-not-run-twice
sequences.note: notif.action is the one acked notif message: a repeated id gets the first ack again and is not run again

sequences.name: notif-action-is-not-resent-after-reconnect
sequences.note: the sender never re-sends a notif.action, so a new connection starts clean; if a buggy sender did repeat the id, the receiver's memory (it is stored) acks it and does not run it again

sequences.name: notif-post-after-reconnect-needs-the-hellos-again
sequences.note: a new connection starts before_hello: a post before the hellos is bad_request and closes with 1002 (nothing is remembered, nothing re-sent)

sequences.name: notif-sync-removes-the-rest
sequences.note: posts A and B, then a sync listing only A: the receiver reports the list, and the app removes the others (see syncDiff[] in notif.json)

sequences.name: notif-invalid-post-keeps-the-connection-open
sequences.note: a bad post gets an error with its id as ref and the connection stays open; the next good one is shown

sequences.name: notif-status-then-icon-then-post
sequences.note: the order the phone sends after the hellos: status, icon, sync, then posts

sequences.name: media-is-not-in-the-dedup-memory
sequences.note: a repeated id of an ephemeral media message is processed again: no ack, no ignore_duplicate

sequences.name: media-status-change-needs-no-new-hello
sequences.note: the four switches travel in media.status: one hello, then any number of statuses

sequences.name: media-capability-changes-with-a-new-hello
sequences.note: the latest hello of the sender decides: without media in it the messages are dropped silently, with it they are accepted again

sequences.name: media-cmd-is-not-resent-after-reconnect
sequences.note: a media.cmd is ephemeral: after a reconnect nothing comes before the hellos, and a new one is processed like any other

sequences.name: media-image-before-state
sequences.note: an image goes out before the first state that uses its hash; both are plain ephemeral messages

sequences.name: media-invalid-state-keeps-the-connection-open
sequences.note: a bad_request is an error with a ref; the connection stays open and the next state works

sequences.name: presence-not-sent-without-capability
sequences.note: a phone that does not list presence (a 0.1.x phone) is never a source of presence for a 0.2.0 PC: whatever it sends is dropped, silently

sequences.name: presence-dropped-when-feature-off-is-silent
sequences.note: the capability is per latest hello: a phone that sends a new hello without presence is dropped silently again, and accepted when it lists it again

sequences.name: presence-is-not-acked-or-deduplicated
sequences.note: ephemeral: the same id twice is processed twice, with no ack

sequences.name: presence-snapshot-replaces-pause
sequences.note: each presence is a whole snapshot: the next one without pause means not paused (the receiver keeps what the LAST one said)

sequences.name: presence-forgotten-on-close
sequences.note: a new connection starts before_hello with nothing known about the peer: the viewer forgets the pause (the app's own memory is a unit test); the first snapshot after the new hellos replaces it

sequences.name: ring-not-sent-without-capability
sequences.note: a phone whose hello does not list ring answers a ring.start that reaches it anyway with error disabled (the PC never sends one: it checks the capability first)

sequences.name: ring-capability-follows-the-switch
sequences.note: the phone's latest hello decides: ring on, off, on

sequences.name: ring-start-is-not-resent-after-reconnect
sequences.note: never re-sent: nothing comes before the new hellos. If a repeat did come, the remembered id would be acked and nothing would ring twice

sequences.name: ring-start-is-acked-once
sequences.note: acked and de-duplicated like notif.action: a repeat of the id gets the same ack and does not ring again

sequences.name: ring-status-is-ephemeral
sequences.note: not acked, not de-duplicated: the same id twice is processed twice

sequences.name: ring-disabled-error-is-not-remembered
sequences.note: an error disabled or rate_limited does not put the id in the de-duplication memory (the PC never re-sends, but a repeat after the switch is on again must ring)

timers.name: no-hello-10-and-a-half-seconds-closes-with-1002
timers.note: no error message is sent: the connection is just closed with 1002

timers.name: hello-accepted-then-silence-is-not-this-timers-business
timers.note: liveness after the handshake is WebSocket ping/pong, see the architecture

closeCodes.name: going-away-1001
closeCodes.note: not in the close table: handled like 1000

closeCodes.name: internal-error-1011
closeCodes.note: not in the close table: handled like 1000

closeCodes.name: protocol-error-1002-from-peer
closeCodes.note: the backoff stops a persistent bug from becoming a fast loop

closeCodes.name: replaced-4001
closeCodes.note: another connection took over this device: only reconnect on the next user action or network change

closeCodes.name: stable-60-s-then-network-error
closeCodes.note: the hello had been accepted for exactly 60 s: the backoff goes back to its first step

closeCodes.name: stable-an-hour-then-replaced-4001
closeCodes.note: it was a stable connection, so the backoff is reset even though no automatic reconnect follows

closeCodes.name: closed-at-once-after-an-accepted-hello
closeCodes.note: a peer that accepts the hello and closes at once must not turn the reconnect into a fast loop

closeCodes.name: no-hello-ever-accepted-1002
closeCodes.note: the 10 s hello timeout: the socket was open, but no hello was accepted, so it counts for nothing

closeCodes.name: open-10-minutes-but-hello-accepted-5-s-ago
closeCodes.note: the 60 s are counted from the accepted hello, not from the moment the socket opened
